skill.name: baoyu-danger-gemini-web
skill.description: Generate Gemini text and images through the reverse-engineered Gemini Web API, including vision prompts, reference images, and multi-turn sessions.
skill.summary: Generate Gemini text and images with authenticated Web API sessions.
skill.author: jimliu

security_audit.summary: Most low and medium static matches are false positives from documented Google endpoints, relative imports, template literals, configuration reads, and normal session storage. Confirmed risks include cached authentication-cookie access, shell process execution for WSL detection, browser cookie reuse, and an output filename path escape; the skill should not be published until these are addressed.

remediation.issue: Shell execution in WSL path detection
remediation.suggestion: Replace execSync with a non-shell process API using fixed argument arrays, or use a native path conversion library. Validate all command output before reuse.

Require explicit consent immediately before access, use a dedicated browser profile, restrict cookie use to Google hosts, protect cache files with restrictive permissions, and never log cookie values.
Reduce the filename to path.basename, reject separators and traversal segments, and verify the final resolved path remains inside the selected output directory before writing.
Use an OS credential store or encrypted storage where available, minimize token lifetime, and provide a clear command to revoke and delete cached credentials.
Document the account and service risks, obtain user confirmation before network or upload operations, and review Google terms and endpoint stability before distribution.

semantic_findings.title: Authenticated Browser Session Reuse
semantic_findings.description: The client discovers an existing Chrome debugging session, retrieves Google cookies through CDP, and persists them for authenticated Gemini requests. This can grant the skill access to an active Google account session.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The source directly discovers a running browser, calls Network.getCookies for Google domains, and returns the cookie values for later authenticated requests.

semantic_findings.title: Output Filename Path Escape
semantic_findings.description: Image.save joins the resolved output directory with a filename without constraining the filename to a basename. A caller-supplied filename containing traversal segments could write outside the intended directory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The destination is built with path.join from a caller-influenced filename, and no basename check or resolved-path containment check is present before writeFile.

content.value_statement: Connects AI workflows to Gemini Web generation without a separate API integration. Produces text, images, vision responses, and multi-turn results from a command-line interface.
actual_capabilities: Sends text prompts to supported Gemini Web models.
Generates images and saves returned image files locally.
Accepts reference images for vision and image variation workflows.
Maintains multi-turn conversations through named session files.
Loads authenticated cookies from a local cache or Chrome CDP session.
limitations: Requires an authenticated Google Gemini Web session and supported browser tooling.
Uses reverse-engineered web endpoints that can change without notice.
Does not provide official Google API guarantees, quotas, or service-level support.
Local cookie and session files require careful permission and account isolation.

use_cases.title: Prototype Visual Concepts
use_cases.description: Generate concept images, variations, and visual references while exploring an early creative direction.

use_cases.title: Run Vision Experiments
use_cases.description: Send reference images with focused prompts to compare descriptions, transformations, and multimodal responses.

use_cases.title: Add Gemini to Workflows
use_cases.description: Call Gemini text or image generation from an existing automation workflow through a simple command-line interface.

prompt_templates.title: Simple Text Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a concise explanation of [topic] for [audience]. Use clear headings and three practical examples.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a detailed image of [subject] in [style]. Use [lighting], [color direction], and a [composition] suitable for [use].

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Reference
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the reference image and describe its subject, composition, lighting, and visual style. List three specific improvement options.

prompt_templates.title: Continue a Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Continue the current conversation. Use the previous constraints, then produce [requested result] with these checks: [check one], [check two].

output_examples.input: Create a square editorial illustration of a quiet mountain research station at dawn.
output_examples.output: A generated image is saved to the selected output directory, with the returned title and image metadata available to the caller.

output_examples.input: Describe the attached product photo and suggest three improvements for its presentation.
output: The response identifies the product, framing, lighting, and visible distractions.
It suggests three concrete changes to improve clarity and presentation.

best_practices: Use a dedicated Google account and browser profile for this integration.
Review prompts, reference images, and upload destinations before each run.
Keep cached cookies and session files outside shared directories with restrictive permissions.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill with a shared browser profile containing unrelated accounts.
Do not send confidential prompts or images without confirming the destination and retention expectations.
Do not rely on reverse-engineered endpoints for critical production guarantees.

faq.question: What does this skill generate?
faq.answer: It generates Gemini text responses, images, vision responses, and multi-turn conversation results.

faq.question: Does it require a Google login?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses an authenticated Gemini Web session and may load cookies through a dedicated Chrome profile.

faq.question: Which inputs can I provide?
faq.answer: You can provide prompt text, prompt files, reference images, model options, and a session identifier.

faq.question: Is this an official Google API client?
faq.answer: No. It uses reverse-engineered Gemini Web endpoints and can break when the web service changes.

faq.question: Where are sessions stored?
faq.answer: Sessions and cached authentication data are stored in the configured Gemini Web data directory.

faq.question: Can I use it in production?
faq.answer: Use it only after reviewing account, privacy, endpoint stability, and credential-storage risks for your environment.
